title: Aurora request canvas and probe notes
content:
Executive snapshot:
This note bundles 15 recent field conversations (B2B: mid-market to enterprise) into a compact canvas of asks, quickfix patches, and low-effort probes. Goal: identify 2–3 high-leverage runtime/product changes we can ship as small experiments within 6–8 weeks, and a separate set of engineering investigations for Dedicated/Private customers.

Method and sample framing:
- Period: 2029-06 to 2029-08
- Source: customer calls (recorded), support tickets flagged `runtime-impact`, top-10 customers by monthly token spend, partner engineering syncs
- Quick synth: grouped signals into technical friction, visibility/observability gaps, and feature asks (routing/cost controls).

Top signals (raw):
1) "Embedding drift" pain: customers with heavy embedding use are noticing embeddings quality variability after model rollouts and quantization switches; common request: clear versioning per-index and a simple diff report when model/quantization changes occur.
2) KV cache TTL and manual invalidation: teams want per-route or per-request KV TTLs and an endpoint to invalidate prefixes (not global). Frequent ask for a lightweight admin API.
3) Routing fallbacks + cost transparency: when we fallback to cheaper variant, customers want automated cost delta notifications and per-request lineage (which model handled the request).
4) Autoscale knob clarity for Dedicated: unclear burst capacity accounting leads to unexpected throttles; ask for a visible forecast and what-ifs UI.
5) Quick visibility for cost/latency tradeoffs: product teams want a small console widget that simulates token-cost under different batching/quant/kv settings for a given route.
6) Minor but sticky UX: lack of per-prompt deterministic rollout tags; customers use various tagging conventions and want our built-in tag + outcome comparison.

Representative customer quotes:
- "We switched to 4-bit for an index and suddenly Rerank precision dropped — we had no record of the switch in our console." — search infra lead, fintech
- "Our support folks want to blow away a single conversation cache key when it goes weird, not flush everything." — PM, conversational AI startup
- "If you fall back to the smaller model, tell us how much we're saving in $ and the latency delta so we can make informed tradeoffs." — platform eng, mid-market

Prioritized probe candidates (fast experiments / 6–8 weeks):
A) KV-invalidation micro-API (low risk): implement a new admin endpoint: POST /admin/kv/invalidate {prefix, route, scope}. Start with Hosted-only and a soft-rate limit. Deliverable: docs, dashboard action, telemetry. Rationale: high request frequency, low infra complexity.
B) Model-change audit event + diff digest (medium effort): emit structured events when model variant or quantization profile changes for a user's route. Attach a small nightly digest email / console banner for affected customers. Rationale: reduces surprise regressions; moderate implementation (config + event plumbing).
C) Route cost simulator widget (prototype UI + heuristics) (medium effort): front-end prototype that estimates per-route token cost under three profiles (default, aggressive-batching, quantized-variant). Backed by a simple heuristic engine using recent token distribution. Rationale: high product value for customers balancing cost/latency.

Lower-priority / engineering investigations (8–16+ weeks):
D) Per-request TTL semantics: design exploration for TTL enforcement with KV cache shards; tradeoffs: correctness vs. throughput. Needs SRE + runtime design doc.
E) Dedicated autoscale accounting transparency: deeper infra work to expose burst budgeting and forecast hooks; requires cross-team roadmap with Dedicated infra.
F) Model lineage in traces: instrument tracer spans to include model variant metadata across retries/fallbacks; small changes but careful tracing compatibility testing required.

Quick fixes and low-friction wins (2–3 weeks):
- Add a conservative console note for deployments that have changed quantization or model weight hash — include link to model catalog entry.
- Support-team playbook: how to manually flag and notify customers when we detect a change in serving baseline for their route (auto-attach recent perf metrics).
- Expose a single-button admin cache-clear in the console restricted by RBAC (Hosted only) — log the action.

Impact-rough RICE-ish heuristics (qualitative):
- KV-invalidation API: Reach = high (many small teams), Impact = medium-high, Confidence = 70%, Effort = low
- Model-change audit/digest: Reach = medium, Impact = high (avoids regressions), Confidence = 60%, Effort = medium
- Cost-simulator widget: Reach = medium-high, Impact = medium-high (helps tradeoff decisions), Confidence = 65%, Effort = medium

Open questions / risks:
- Security/abuse of admin cache-invalidation endpoint: need RBAC + rate limit discussion; potential for accidental data loss.
- Signal fidelity: how do we robustly detect a user-visible regression vs. noisy eval variance? (Need evaluation/ops criteria.)
- Dedicated customers will want SLAs around any new console-only features — coordinate with sales/legal.

Next steps (owner & ETA):
- Week 1: Align with runtime eng on KV invalidation feasibility (owner: Ethan Park) 
- Week 2: Prototype admin endpoint + internal integration tests (owner: Jordan Li) 
- Week 3: UX mock for console button and simulator (owner: Maya Singh) 
- Week 4–6: Pilot with 3 customers (one fintech, one marketplace, one AI startup). Collect qualitative feedback and telemetry (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Notes to self / ancillary ideas:
- Consider a lightweight "model-change flag" in the SDK that allows customers to opt-in to receiving regressions alerts; could be an opt-in Beta.
- Capture two canonical repro prompts per customer when we detect a drop in rerank/precision — store alongside event to speed debugging.
- Map legal requirements for Private deployments: some customers cannot accept auto-notifications that include model internals.

Appendix: telemetry heuristics to collect during pilots (short):
- #cache-invalidate-requests by customer and prefix
- % routes with model-version change events in last 7 days
- avg latency/cost delta when fallback occurs (per-route)
- support escalations mentioning "cache" or "model change" within 48h of any config change

If this looks sensible I'll draft a single-page PRD for the KV-invalidation micro-API and a companion UX ticket for the console action. Feedback welcome — please add inline comments or ping me on slack in #cs-runtime-echoes.
